assessment.nobel_worthiness: A genuinely new idea with deep consequences: trapping atoms at the magic wavelength so that the light shift cancels, giving optical clocks with fractional uncertainty far below the caesium standard. It rests on atomic structure and polarizability physics I know well, and it opens fundamental tests (constants, relativistic redshift across millimetres) that nobody expected a few decades ago.
assessment.attribution: Katori made the proposal of magic-wavelength lattice trapping and the early Sr demonstrations; Jun Ye's group brought the clock to the 1e-18 regime and to the many-body regime. Two names give a clean, fair configuration; the supplied credit does not obviously need a third person.
assessment.maturity: Independently realized and advanced in Tokyo, Boulder, Paris, Germany, China and elsewhere; comparisons of clocks agree at the 1e-18 level and the redefinition of the second is in discussion. The physics is stable and the recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Hall's 2005 recognition for the frequency comb makes some members feel this field is partly honoured already.
The share between the theoretical proposal and the Boulder realization could be argued, and other lattice-clock groups (and ion clocks) are not credited.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cirac and Zoller proposed the trapped-ion quantum gate and the framework for quantum simulation with cold atoms and ions, linking atomic physics to quantum information. The ideas are original, clear and have shaped two decades of experiments; this is quantum mechanics put to work on the boundary question of what we can control coherently.
assessment.attribution: The pair is the unambiguous core of the theory proposals, with a compact two-person credit. Experimental realization belongs to others (Wineland, Blatt, Monroe), so the prize would be for theory and I would want that stated clearly.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by many ion and neutral-atom platforms, and the field is mature. Wineland's 2012 prize overlaps in part, which tempers the novelty of a new prize but not the importance of the theory.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2012 prize for controlling single quantum systems and with entangled-photon recognition in 2022.
The candidate is broad (gates, simulation), and the decisive paper for each part may be different.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The quantum spin Hall effect and Z2 topological insulators opened a new class of matter whose edge and surface states are protected by symmetry. The theory of Kane and Mele was original and was confirmed quickly in experiment, which is the combination I look for. I defer somewhat to colleagues in condensed matter on the ranking against other topological work.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the decisive theoretical prediction; Molenkamp's group gave the first experimental observation in HgTe quantum wells (with Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang as the HgTe prediction, not credited here). The three-name configuration is workable but leaves out important figures.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced in many materials and probed by several techniques; the interpretation is stable. The 2016 prize recognized topological phase transitions, so this is a next step rather than a repeat, and timing is good.
uncertainties: Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang and the 3D topological insulator experiments (Hasan, Kane-Moore-Balents) are not in the credited set, so attribution is open.
A duplicate candidate of this physics exists on the list and the choice of name sets is not settled.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Geometric phases and the Aharonov-Bohm effect say something conceptually deep about quantum mechanics: that potentials and paths in parameter space matter beyond local forces. They are simple to explain and appear everywhere, from molecules to optics to solids. This is the kind of fundamental, non-technological discovery I value.
assessment.attribution: Aharonov and Bohm (Bohm is deceased) and Berry are the natural names; a living pair gives a clean configuration, though Pancharatnam and Bohm's earlier contributions complicate the story. Berry's phase paper is the clear key insight.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed in countless experiments, long established and textbook. If anything the recognition is late rather than premature, which also raises the question of why it has not come earlier.
uncertainties: Bohm's death means the Aharonov-Bohm effect cannot be fully credited, and Pancharatnam's priority for the geometric phase in optics is a known allocation issue.
Whether the committee would treat this as a discovery or an interpretation of quantum mechanics is a matter of taste.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of flat bands at the magic angle and the discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states in twisted bilayer graphene created moire quantum matter, a new tunable platform. It is surprising and scientifically fertile, though I am not an expert in condensed matter and defer to colleagues on its relative weight.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the theoretical prediction; Jarillo-Herrero's group made the decisive 2018 observations. This is a theory-plus-experiment pairing that suits a fair three-person split, though other groups also contributed.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced across many laboratories, but the nature of the superconductivity and the correlated states is still being debated, so interpretation is not yet settled. It may be a little early.
uncertainties: The mechanism of superconductivity in twisted bilayers is unresolved.
Credit questions remain for other contributors (for example Cao, Fatemi, and earlier theory of moire bands) who are not in the supplied set.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Electromagnetically induced transparency is a beautiful quantum interference effect in atoms, and the slow and stopped light that followed was unexpected. I understand the underlying atomic physics well; it is conceptually clean and has become a standard tool in quantum optics and memory experiments.
assessment.attribution: Harris established the theory and early demonstration of EIT; Hau's group achieved extreme slow light in a Bose condensate and stopped light. Imamoglu contributed to the theory of EIT-related ideas but I would prefer the two-person split from the list.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed in many laboratories and used for quantum memories and sensing. The effect is old enough to be mature, though the prize case rests on whether it is seen as a discovery of nature or a technique.
uncertainties: Boller, Imamoglu and Field's 1991 observation and Kocharovskaya's earlier work on coherent population trapping complicate priority.
Possible concern that the impact is more technical than conceptual.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The discovery of a diffuse flux of astrophysical neutrinos with IceCube opened neutrino astronomy and was confirmed by the later association with a blazar. It is a clean new window on the high-energy universe, and a true discovery of something nobody could predict in detail. I am less able to judge the details and defer to astrophysics colleagues.
assessment.attribution: A large collaboration of hundreds, with Halzen as leader and the early drivers of the detector concept. Karle and Spiering are leaders in construction and early analysis. The prize rule of three is hard here and the allocation is unclear.
assessment.maturity: Independently supported by ANTARES-type and later IceCube analyses of different channels, plus the 2018 TXS 0506+056 association, but source identification is still limited, so the field is maturing rather than complete.
uncertainties: Original AMANDA pioneers and the many collaboration members make the choice of three people contestable.
The origin of the diffuse flux is still not understood.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Evidence for a nanohertz gravitational-wave background from pulsar timing arrays is a striking result about the Universe, open a new frequency band. It is conceptually clean (timing correlations following the Hellings-Downs pattern), but the evidence level is moderate.
assessment.attribution: A long effort by several collaborations (NANOGrav, EPTA, PPTA, CPTA); Manchester, Kramer and McLaughlin are leaders of the field, but the decisive discovery is a joint result, so attribution is unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Several independent arrays reported consistent signals in 2023, yet the significance is only about 3-4 sigma and the source (supermassive black-hole binaries versus new physics) is undetermined. It is probably premature.
uncertainties: Significance is below the discovery standard; amplitude is higher than some models expect.
Attribution across four collaborations is not resolved by the supplied names.
